description: Append-only compact index of continuous workflow simulation session records. Raw compact evidence remains immutable; post-hoc integrity assessments may exclude records from objective use without rewriting raw metrics or artifacts.
append_policy: Add one immutable workflow_session record per executed baseline or treatment session. Never reuse a session ID or overwrite its compact evidence. A reusable baseline-pool identity is the frozen protocol fingerprint plus replicate, not execution date; the fingerprint binds fixture snapshot, task/verifier bytes, baseline substrate, runtime/model condition, and isolation policy. Completed workflow-simulation reproduction records must use sequential one-task-at-a-time prompt delivery, lazy future-prompt materialization, controller-only verifier assets, verifier integrity hashes, and seed-origin concealment. Create comparisons only after the relevant baseline and treatment records for the same pool exist. Normal baselines require objective acceptance; a reviewed primary-objective hard baseline may remain failed and still anchor token-usage comparison when its hard-lane policy fields and compact artifacts pass integrity checks. Supersede rather than delete historical results. A post-hoc integrity assessment may change status or objective eligibility only when the raw metrics/artifacts are preserved and the reason/evidence are recorded.

baseline_pool.identity_policy: frozen-protocol-and-replicate; execution date is metadata only

install.policy: Run Codex from a fresh lane-specific CODEX_HOME with auth only, no MCP servers, no global instructions, no hooks, no skills/plugins, isolated HOME/PYTHONUSERBASE/XDG/TMPDIR, and a preflight artifact proving empty MCP config.

reset.policy: Delete the lane-specific Codex home and run-local HOME/PYTHONUSERBASE/XDG/TMPDIR before each run; verify no stale indexes or generated profile files survive.

registry_entry.notes: Canonical Codex CLI no-MCP substrate baseline. Codex native shell/edit/file/git/verifier operations are allowed; MCP, retrieval, compression, memory, token-saving add-ons, global instructions, hooks, skills/plugins, and warm indexes are forbidden.

runtime.isolation_policy: fresh lane-specific Codex home/tool data; sequential one-task prompt delivery; concealed tests removed before model-visible root commit

baseline_pool_reference.comparison_policy: paired baseline and treatment must share this baseline pool fingerprint and replicate

task_sequence.reset_policy: reset source checkout, profile home, tool state, indexes, caches, generated config, and agent home before the lane; preserve repository, thread, tool, index, cache, and agent state across every sequential prompt

leakage_controls.model_writable_surface: target repository plus isolated model-output directory
remaining_limitations: Future regression code is present from lane start, while future prompts and concealed acceptance assets remain controller-only.

hard_lane_policy.primary_objective_use: A failed but well-formed bare run may be the frozen token-usage baseline when all provider turns operationally complete, every task is agent-declared complete, provider usage and compact artifacts are intact, and verifier failure is preserved in the record.
hard_lane_policy.outperformance_rule: A treatment is better when it improves verified correctness or matches verified correctness with fewer provider tokens; token-efficiency claims require no worse correctness and fewer tokens.
hard_lane_policy.claim_boundary: Agent-declared completion and verifier-confirmed correctness are separate fields.
